text: What is a lambda in C++, and what is the difference between capturing a variable by value and by reference?
key_points: a nameless function written inline, kept in auto|capture by value copies the variable at that moment|later changes outside are not seen by a copy|capture by reference uses the real variable, so changes are visible both ways

text: When would you use a deque instead of a vector?
key_points: deque has O(1) push and pop at both ends|vector front insert or erase is O(n) because everything shifts|both can be indexed|growing a vector may reallocate and invalidate iterators

text: How do map and unordered_map differ, and what surprising thing does operator[] do?
key_points: map keeps keys sorted, O(log n) per operation|unordered_map uses hashing, O(1) average, no ordering|operator[] inserts a default value when the key is missing|use find or count to test membership without inserting

text: What must a sort comparator guarantee, and why is using <= in it a bug?
key_points: it answers whether a must come strictly before b|needs a strict weak ordering|<= claims a comes before itself, so sort can misbehave or crash|use < and break ties explicitly; stable_sort keeps the order of equal elements

text: What do lower_bound and upper_bound return in a sorted array?
key_points: lower_bound is the first element not smaller than x|upper_bound is the first element greater than x|the gap between them is how often x appears|for a missing value both are the same position, and end() must not be dereferenced

text: How does binary search on the answer work, and what must be true about the check function?
key_points: search over possible answers, not array positions|check(mid) must be monotonic: false then true, or the reverse|example: smallest speed that finishes all work in time|move low or high according to the check; the bound update must not loop forever

text: What is a binary heap, and how is it stored in an array?
key_points: a complete binary tree where each parent is at least (max-heap) or at most (min-heap) its children|stored in an array with no pointers|children of index i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2|top is O(1), push and pop are O(log n)

text: What makes a recursive solution correct, and what happens if the base case is missing?
key_points: a base case that stops the recursion|each call moves closer to the base case|a missing base case overflows the call stack|very deep recursion can hit the stack limit and is safer as a loop

text: Why is naive recursive Fibonacci slow, and how does memoisation fix it?
key_points: the same subproblems are solved again and again|two calls per level gives about 2 to the n calls|memoisation stores each answer the first time|then each value is computed once, so O(n)

text: How does a stack help you check whether the brackets in an expression are balanced?
key_points: push every opening bracket|each closing bracket must match the one on top|the stack must be empty at the end|one pass, O(n)

text: How do you detect a cycle in a linked list?
key_points: a slow pointer moves one step and a fast pointer two|inside a cycle the fast pointer gains one step each move, so they meet|if fast reaches null there is no cycle|O(n) time and O(1) extra space (Floyd)

text: What are preorder, inorder and postorder traversals of a binary tree, and how do they differ?
key_points: preorder visits node, left, right|inorder visits left, node, right|postorder visits left, right, node|same walk, only the moment of visiting the node changes

text: Why does level order traversal need a queue, and how do you process one level at a time?
key_points: BFS visits nodes level by level|a queue holds the nodes waiting, children join at the back|read the queue size at the start of a level to know how many nodes it has|DFS uses recursion or a stack instead

text: What is the difference between the height and the depth of a node in a binary tree?
key_points: height is how far down the deepest leaf below it is|depth is how far it is from the root|height is computed bottom-up after the children return|depth is passed down top-down; counting in nodes or edges changes the numbers by one

text: How do you compute the diameter of a binary tree in linear time?
key_points: the diameter is the longest path between any two nodes|it need not pass through the root|at each node the best path bending there is left height plus right height|return the height upwards and keep the maximum; recomputing heights at every node would be O(N squared)

text: How do you find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary tree?
key_points: search both subtrees|if both sides report a target, the current node is the LCA|if only one side reports, pass it up (a node can be its own ancestor)|O(N) time; in a BST use the ordering to go left or right

text: What is the binary search tree property, and why does it make search fast?
key_points: every key in the left subtree is smaller and in the right subtree larger|one comparison discards a whole subtree|cost is the height, not N|sorted insertion order degenerates the tree into a list; inorder traversal is sorted

text: How do you delete a node from a binary search tree, and what are the cases?
key_points: leaf: simply remove it|one child: replace the node with its child|two children: copy the inorder successor's key up and delete it from the right subtree|the BST property is kept in every case

text: What is the exchange argument, and how does it show that a greedy order is safe?
key_points: take any solution that is not in greedy order|swap two neighbours into greedy order|show the swap does not make the answer worse|repeat until the solution equals the greedy one; example: shortest job first minimises total waiting

text: In activity selection, why do we sort the activities by end time and not by start time?
key_points: finishing earliest leaves the largest remaining time|no other first choice can do better|sorting by start fails: one long activity can block many short ones|then keep each next activity that starts after the last chosen one ends

text: Why is the greedy approach correct for fractional knapsack but not for 0/1 knapsack?
key_points: fractional: items can be cut, so best value per weight first is optimal|0/1: items are whole, so a high ratio item can strand capacity|a small counterexample exists where two lower-ratio items beat it|0/1 knapsack needs dynamic programming

text: How does a hash table store and find a key, and what is a collision?
key_points: a hash function turns the key into a bucket index|lookup is O(1) on average|a collision is two keys landing in the same bucket|handled by chaining (a list per bucket) or open addressing

text: When would you use unordered_set instead of set?
key_points: unordered_set is hash based: O(1) average, no ordering|set is sorted: O(log n)|use unordered_set when you only ask whether a value has been seen|use set when you need order, for example lower_bound or sorted output

text: Numbers arrive one at a time, and at any moment you must report the k-th largest so far. How would you do it, and what does it cost?
key_points: keep a min-heap holding the k largest values|its top is the k-th largest so far|push each new number and pop the smallest if the size exceeds k|O(log k) per number instead of sorting everything

text: Given an array and a target, how would you find two numbers that add up to the target?
key_points: store values you have seen in a hash map|for each x check whether target minus x was seen|O(n) time instead of O(n squared) brute force|if the array is sorted, two pointers from the ends also works

text: Someone checks whether a tree is a BST by comparing each node only with its two children. Why is that wrong, and how would you fix it?
key_points: a node must also be in range of all its ancestors|counter-example: a large value deep in the left subtree of a small root|pass down a valid low and high range|or check that the inorder traversal is strictly increasing

text: You are given the preorder and inorder traversals of a binary tree. How can you rebuild the tree?
key_points: the first preorder element is the root|its position in inorder splits the left and right parts|recurse on the two parts|a map from value to inorder index keeps it fast; inorder is needed to tell left from right

text: A station has arrival and departure times for many trains. How would you find the minimum number of platforms needed?
key_points: only the number of trains present at the same time matters|sort arrivals and departures separately|walk both: add one at an arrival, remove one at a departure|decide how a tie (arrival at the departure time) is handled; the maximum count is the answer

text: For every number in an array you must find the next greater number to its right. How would you do it in one pass?
key_points: keep a stack of indices still waiting for a bigger value|when a larger number arrives, pop and answer the smaller ones|every index is pushed and popped once, so O(n)|brute force would be O(n squared)

text: A recursive minimum-depth function returns 0 for a null child and so gives the wrong answer for a node with only one child. Why, and how do you fix it?
key_points: a null child returning 0 makes the node look like a leaf|minimum depth must end at a real leaf|only descend into the child that exists|maximum depth does not have this problem
